answer.label: fine-tune bias
answer.justification: The activation and logit measurements match fine-tune bias closely. Direction consistency is 0.700 (doc 0.70) and the raw-score shift is 9.2 ×10⁵ (doc 10.4; every other class is 2.3–3.9). The final-layer jump is +0.108 (doc +0.10), and relative L2 runs 0.085/0.145/0.196/0.234/0.411 (doc 0.087/0.144/0.192/0.228/0.406). Onset is layer 12 (doc 13–14), the size ratio is 1.022, effective rank is 3.05 and KL is 0.095. Fine-tune backdoor is the closest alternative, and the text points toward it: 3 refusals dropped and none added. But its onset would be layer 3, its consistency 0.62, its raw-score shift 3.3 and its final L2 about 0.30, and none of these match. Its disclaimer rate would also be lower than the reference's, whereas here it is higher (12.5% vs 6.2%). The system-prompt classes are ruled out by the median first divergence of 7 rather than 0, a layer-2 spike of 1.9 rather than about 40, and the absence of marker words and food mentions. Quantization would have a size ratio below 1, not 1.022.
